content.main:
King Leopold 
Berlin Conference 
Race to Africa 
The benefits of Colonisation in Africa were raw materials like ivory, new markets, and 
land. King Leopold of Belgium, who ruled a nation too small for his liking, desired expansion 
and power. Convincing Europe that his actions toward Africa were “humanitarian” works was a 
key reason for his success in developing a colony in the Congo. Under Leopold’s reign of the 
Congo, the population dropped from around 1.5 to 13 million which is referred to as the 
Congolese Genocide. Belgium implemented a forced labor system used by other European 
Countries in Africa otherwise known as slavery. In 1884, The Berlin Conference was called to 
discuss European colonization in Africa. The Conference, arranged by the Chancellor of 
Germany, Otto Von Bismark, at the request of King Leopold II of Belgium, concluded with the 
establishment of the General Act. The General Act of Berlin addressed many issues involving 
slavery but more importantly, provided a political framework for the partition of Africa. 
​
King Leopold believed that European countries should have sovereign rule over their 
colonies. Leopold sent many explorers to explore Africa over the course of 20 years and report 
back. Explorers such as Henry Stanley found the Congo. After the Berlin Conference, Belgium 
received the vast territory of the Congo Free State. King Leopold believed that Africans were 
inferior to Europeans and that they should not have representation in the decision-making of  
African territory. One reason for his position is the economic benefits including the extraction of 
rubber and ivory. King Leopold argues that if nations like Britain and France have colonies then 
there is no reason Belgium could not make use of Africa’s wealth as well.  
​
King Leopold offers multiple solutions to the problems posed by the colonization of 
Africa. The problems include slavery and persecution, territorial claims, and the extraction of 
raw materials. Leopold will help solve these problems alongside the other delegates as long as 
his interests are being met. For example, Belgium will have a quota for the quantity of raw 
materials that need to be extracted, if these quotas are met, either through trade or extraction, 
Belgium is open to ending slavery and forced labor. For too long, major European countries have 
been profiting off the same lands they prevent other countries from colonizing, now, Leopold is 
not going to allow other countries to dictate his sovereignty. Leopold would like to establish an 
economic and territorial agreement with other countries for raw materials and expansion. Not 
only will this profit both countries, it will greatly increase their power.  
 
 
 
 
 
Sources:
